oil.summary: Crude prices edged marginally higher on the day — WTI +0.13% to $68.78, Brent +0.46% to $72.13 — but the headline story is the brutal one-month collapse of roughly 26-28%. RBOB gasoline cratered 4.91% on the session, while heating oil bucked the trend with a 2.34% gain. The market is digesting two competing forces: Citi flagging a potential Brent slide to $60 as Hormuz traffic normalises, while OPEC production rebounds as Gulf producers restore shut-in barrels. Iran's stated position that its blockade continues until strikes cease, offset by active US-Iran Doha talks, is keeping traders cautious. Russia's refining crisis deepens — Ukrainian drone strikes have forced one of the world's largest oil producers to seek jet fuel imports — while India's role as an intermediary supplier draws scrutiny from its own government.
drivers: Citi projects Brent at $60 on Hormuz normalisation; OPEC June output rebounds but Gulf supply remains below pre-disruption levels
Iran maintains blockade posture; US-Iran Doha talks ongoing, leaving geopolitical risk premium uncertain
Russia's refinery capacity crippled by Ukrainian strikes, forcing jet fuel and gasoline imports; US temporarily eases Russia sanctions to cap prices, straining European allies

gas.summary: Natural gas markets posted modest gains: Henry Hub rose 1.53% to $3.245/MMBtu, extending a quiet week that is flat on net (+0.43%). TTF added 0.53% to €44.25/MWh, though the European benchmark remains down 9.44% on the month despite a sharp 8.50% weekly surge, suggesting residual short-covering or supply-security buying tied to the broader Middle East and Russia disruption narrative. Gas-specific headline flow today is thin; the most relevant news touching the sector is the DOJ's directive urging states to enforce fuel price-gouging laws amid elevated consumer energy costs. No LNG, storage, or weather-specific headlines were available in today's feed.
drivers: Henry Hub +1.53% on the session; weekly and monthly moves modest, suggesting no acute supply shock priced in domestically
TTF weekly surge of 8.50% points to European buyers pricing in residual supply-security risk from Middle East and Russia disruptions
DOJ formally pressing states on fuel price-gouging enforcement signals political sensitivity around elevated retail energy costs

power.summary: The power sector was the day's most acute stress point. PJM — the largest US grid — issued a maximum generation alert for July 3 as a heat wave drove demand toward all-time record territory; reports indicate power prices tripled within PJM, with data centers cited as a compounding load factor alongside the heat event. On the geopolitical side, a drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant briefly lifted oil to a two-week high, underscoring how conflict dynamics are bleeding into power infrastructure risk. EU carbon EUAs firmed 1.56% to $76.32, up 4.64% on the month, consistent with the broader European energy tightness narrative. Ukraine's drone campaign reportedly knocked out 13 Russian power stations in addition to refinery targets, further degrading Russian grid capacity.
drivers: PJM maximum generation alert: extreme heat wave combined with data-center load surge pushed the grid toward an all-time demand record and tripled spot power prices
Drone attack on UAE nuclear power plant added infrastructure risk premium; Ukraine's strikes on 13 Russian power stations escalate conflict impact on energy infrastructure broadly
EU EUAs +1.56% on the day and +4.64% on the month, supported by persistent European energy tightness and TTF's weekly rally
